FL-067.label: Agents move through the file structure of the machine they live in, and the interface shows where every agent is.
FL-067.walk: Ask the agent to move to another folder; the interface shows its new location.
FL-067.observed: Real OpenRouter agent changed WHERE from root to src and docs; Conversation and Farm follow recorded location.

FL-070.label: Image input: paste an image and the agent reviews it.
FL-070.walk: Paste an image; the agent reviews it.
FL-070.observed: Pasted the Farm reference PNG into the real conversation; the model described its contents. Image appears with the answer.

FL-074.label: A new thread starts in a project folder with the location rule in effect; how a thread's project is specified was his open question (maybe configuration).
FL-074.walk: Start a new thread in a folder; the thread shows that folder as its project and the location rule applies.
FL-074.observed: Disposable threads were created in /private/tmp/m3vz-live/work; project and actual WHERE are shown, and the agent moved into docs.

FL-102.label: The Deck: a flashcard stack of terminals, cards colored to match their agents, only one card on top at a time (that project's agent's last response) to interact with, the next card popping up once you respond, ordered purely by which finished first.
FL-102.walk: Answer the top card; it pops and the next card, the earliest to finish, comes up in its agent's color.
FL-102.observed: Three waiting responses became two after sending the oldest edited draft; READY thread 6F2BE493 became next with its color.

FL-104.label: A draft response to the final synthesis that you tweak and fire, after which the stack switches to the agent that has waited longest for your attention.
FL-104.walk: Tweak the draft on the top card and fire it; the stack moves to the agent that has waited longest.
FL-104.observed: Edited the oldest draft to Reply STACK VERIFIED, pressed Enter, observed the next oldest thread and the actual STACK VERIFIED reply.

FL-105.label: An Ableton-like rack: the shipped layout is only version one of the default opinion, and people can easily roll and add their own plugins and visualizers to the views from the ground up.
FL-105.walk: Add a self-authored plugin to the rack; it appears among the modules and works.
FL-105.observed: Imported a self-authored plugin through Library. Its Verify plugin button changed to Plugin verified in its sandboxed module.

FL-110.label: Global or current on every module; current modules switch together with the work.
FL-110.walk: Set two modules to current and select a different project; both switch together while a global one stays.
FL-110.observed: Current-thread Conversation follows selection and global Palace State is available, but two Current modules plus an unchanged global module were not jointly exercised.

FL-111.label: One standard module template that can be dragged and grown or shrunk as much as you want, with a dialogue box for its internal settings, on a very large canvas you can pan and zoom while modules stay the same size.
FL-111.walk: Grow a module far past its starting size, open its settings dialogue, then zoom the canvas out; the module grew without a cap and keeps its size as the canvas zooms.
FL-111.observed: Dragged the plugin from 24x20 to 98x81 grid units, opened its settings, zoomed from 9% to 6%; dimensions stayed 98x81. resize-proof.json.

FL-112.label: Tabs as layers of the same stage; Injection and Graph as ordinary modules; a gear beside the title for rarely changed options.
FL-112.walk: Add a tab, place the Injection module on it, and open the gear beside the title; the tab is a layer of the same stage and the gear holds the rarely changed options.
FL-112.observed: Created Layer 1, added Injection Console from Library, switched to Sheet and opened its title gear.

FL-113.label: A finer, near-continuous background grid, more descriptive well-formatted hover tips, an easy way to create tabs, a much smaller archive button, a model device that is obviously clickable.
FL-113.walk: Hover a control on the stage; a well-formatted descriptive tip appears, the grid behind is near-continuous, a tab can be created easily, the archive button is small, and the model device looks clickable.
FL-113.observed: Fresh canon passed 55 control checks and 43 rendered states; manual layer/gear walk also showed descriptive tooltip, small archive control, model button and continuous grid.

FL-115.label: Attunement to a specific stack beyond global and current.
FL-115.walk: Set a module to a specific stack; it shows it is aligned to that stack, not global or current.
FL-115.observed: Set Spend to Nearest source and Named stack Channel Stack; the settings retain the named stack selection.

FL-116.label: A module not set to global attunes by proximity, measured across tabs (a tab counting one unit) and grid position, ties picked at random, and it shows which thread or stack it is attuned to.
FL-116.walk: Drag a non-global module next to a different thread; its label changes to that thread's name.
FL-116.observed: Named stack selection was exercised; dragging between two distinct thread sources and observing a changed attunement label was not proved.

FL-117.label: A proposed reply prefilled and editable; queued prompts advance on Enter with a scrollable queue.
FL-117.walk: Press Enter in the prefilled proposed reply; the next queued prompt comes up and the queue scrolls.
FL-117.observed: Sent the edited prefilled proposed reply with Enter; waiting count fell 3 to 2 and next oldest response became current.

FL-119.label: A Palace State module holding the general state stats.
FL-119.walk: Open the Palace State module; the general state stats are there, not in the Spend table.
FL-119.observed: Fresh public-install Palace State renders health, memory, queue and learning counts as a distinct module.

FL-120.label: One conversation module with stack and focused modes.
FL-120.walk: Toggle the conversation module between stack and focused; the one module shows the stack or a single thread.
FL-120.observed: Toggled the one Conversation between Focused and Stack. Stack showed oldest-first responses and advanced on send.

FL-127.label: Memories visualized in a cool tesseract-graph style.
FL-127.walk: Open the Memory Graph; memories render as a graph.
FL-127.observed: Fresh browser canon rendered Memory Graph with ten fixture nodes; graph-decluttered screenshot and honest-display.json are local fixture evidence.

FL-141.label: The visualization looks cool but is functional: it changes only when the underlying data or actual running processes change.
FL-141.walk: Leave the visualization open with the system idle; nothing moves until a real process such as a curator pass runs.
FL-141.observed: After live run.completed the ghost has zero active targets; idle meshes remain static. Real finding.started events change target centroid; terminal capture plus progress feed distinguish progress from decoration.

FL-197.label: Spend and Palace state reads use the calling principal; only the configured owner can request the whole Palace.
FL-197.walk: In a verification daemon, open Spend and Palace State and see only that principal's receipts and counts. In a local fixture, compare the configured owner's whole-Palace view. Request scope=palace as the verification principal and see a plain 403. Keep owner-rack captures out of evidence.
FL-197.observed: Fresh real verification principal shows zero scoped counts and owner-only learning message; the full local-owner comparison and plain-403 UI sequence was not performed. Unit isolation checks passed, but do not replace the entire walk.

FL-171.label: A startup and settings option: "Back up conversation transcripts to cloud?"
FL-171.walk: Toggle "Back up conversation transcripts to cloud?" in the settings menu; the backup line changes, and the same question is asked at first startup.
FL-171.observed: Fresh public init asked the transcript-backup question; UI toggle changed to starting 0 records and back to Off. Earlier raw-env fixture save refusal disappeared after canonical initialization.

FL-173.label: Constitution: a warming retry when the Palace is asleep, a "busy, retrying" banner on rate limits, and the banner clears on recovery (gate-day).
FL-173.walk: Start the Harness against a sleeping Palace; a warming line shows, then clears when the Palace answers.
FL-173.observed: Startup visibly checked the Palace and became ready; the Palace was already awake, so waking a sleeping instance was not demonstrated.

FL-178.label: Constitution: a verification identity with its own account and home for tests and scouts (gate verification-identity work).
FL-178.walk: Start the daemon as the verification identity; its Palace shows none of the owner's memories.
FL-178.observed: Fresh public init minted a new non-owner verification identity; its Palace shows zero active memories, candidates, links and queued proposals.

FL-179.label: Constitution: a plain ownership refusal when one identity tries to decide another identity's approval queue item (gate verification-identity work).
FL-179.walk: As the verification identity, decide a card in the owner's approval queue; a plain refusal appears.
FL-179.observed: No owner queue was accessed. A foreign-card refusal was not exercised through a local fixture this walk; fresh scoped empty Palace is context only.

FL-187.label: Two repos, the spine (memory) and the Harness, not a mono repo.
FL-187.walk: List the repositories; the spine and the Harness are two separate git repos.
FL-187.observed: Git roots and distinct GitHub remotes confirmed separate nocturne-harness and nocturne-memory repositories; publication.json records both separate releases.

FL-191.label: The tools and skills Claude Code and Codex use on this machine, pinned to versioned open-source sources.
FL-191.walk: Open the tool inventory; each tool or skill lists the versioned open-source source it is pinned to.
FL-191.observed: Opened Tools & skills inventory in the real thread; versioned Pydantic toolset and skill sources displayed. Actual read, shell, browser and skill calls succeeded.

FL-194.label: The Pydantic toolset and skills as the tool layer.
FL-194.walk: Open the agent's tool list in a thread; the tools come from the Pydantic toolset plus skills, not from pi.
FL-194.observed: Real thread used Pydantic file, shell, browser and skill tools; local data-page read returned copper owl 418. No pi toolset is installed.

FL-195.label: The feature ledger generates coverage reports and requires evidence for the rows affected by a build.
FL-195.walk: Compute the composer fix's impact with --paths and see attunement rows; push a branch touching socket.ts and observe the hook print rows and write impacted.json; observe a DONE handoff without screenshots fail CI, then verify complete evidence passes.
FL-195.observed: Fresh Garden 30-test run exercises impact paths, push bell, DONE-without-evidence refusal and complete-evidence acceptance; hosted impact checks also passed. Screenshot is UI context; garden-checks.log is the tooling proof.

FL-196.label: The rules machine checks citations, frozen law, product vocabulary, seed states and packet precedents.
FL-196.walk: Remove a guard citation on a disposable branch and observe CI fail; change a frozen axiom and observe the freeze step fail; restore both and observe Rules pass. The master ADR check remains red until the owner applies the citation patch.
FL-196.observed: Fresh Garden rules negative tests and full rule export passed; guard-citation and frozen-axiom violations are refused then restored. Screenshot is UI context; garden-checks.log is tooling evidence.

FL-009.label: Record files (history, transcripts) live apart from code so code can be deleted and re-downloaded without losing history.
FL-009.walk: Delete the code folder, reinstall, `nocturne up`; every thread is still there.
FL-009.observed: Fresh no-cache public installation replaced the source runtime. Standard nocturne up restored all three existing disposable threads, including the 14-message original; packaged heartbeat reinstall check also passed.

FL-046.label: A curation animation of its own, blended into the 3D palace.
FL-046.walk: Trigger a curator pass; the 3D Palace view animates the curation as it happens.
FL-046.observed: Live curator progress moved the Palace ghost between actual finding targets before completion; terminal event removes the active ghost. progress-events.json and second-target replay preserve timing.
